articles.title: Modbus RTU temperature and humidity sensor - TSH331

blocks.text: Keeping industrial equipment and technical infrastructure operating reliably often requires continuous monitoring of environmental conditions. Temperature and humidity fluctuations can affect electronics, automation systems, and sensitive equipment, making dependable sensing an important part of modern industrial monitoring. The TSH331 IP54 temperature and humidity sensor provides accurate environmental measurements designed for integration into industrial automation and Modbus-based monitoring systems.

Manufactured by Teracom Ltd., a trusted developer of environmental monitoring and connectivity solutions, the TSH331 is built for stable long-term operation in demanding environments. The sensor combines a precision capacitive humidity sensing element with a bandgap temperature sensor. Internal electronics digitize both signals through a high-quality 12-bit analog-to-digital converter, ensuring consistent and repeatable measurements. With ±3.0% RH accuracy, 12-bit humidity resolution, and 14-bit temperature resolution, the device delivers reliable environmental data across a wide range of industrial and infrastructure applications.

Designed for easy integration, the sensor communicates via RS-485 using the widely adopted Modbus RTU protocol. It supports multi-drop RS-485 networks, allowing multiple sensors to operate on a single bus with individually assigned Modbus addresses - ideal for distributed monitoring in automation systems, telecom facilities, or technical infrastructure.
The IP54 enclosure protects the device against dust and water sprays, while the cable gland and screwless terminal block simplify wiring and speed up installation.
The TSH331 is compatible with:
Industrial PLCs supporting Modbus RTU
SCADA systems and automation controllers
Teracom monitoring modules and controllers
Building management systems (BMS)

Keeping fleet vehicles and assets operating reliably across Australia’s harsh and changing conditions takes more than just GPS tracking. Environmental monitoring plays a growing role in protecting sensitive cargo, improving compliance, and reducing unexpected maintenance costs - and that’s exactly where the TSH202Bcompact humidity and temperature sensor delivers real value.

Manufactured by Teracom Ltd., a trusted specialist in sensing and connectivity solutions, the TSH202B is built for dependable long-term performance in demanding real-world environments. It is a fully calibrated digital sensor that measures both humidity and temperature with high accuracy and excellent stability. The unit combines a unique capacitive humidity sensing element with a band gap temperature sensor, connected to a high-quality 12-bit analog-to-digital converter for fast response and strong signal reliability. With 3.0% RH accuracy, 12-bit humidity resolution, and 14-bit temperature resolution, it delivers consistent data you can rely on across a wide range of fleet applications.

Designed for simple integration, the sensor supports 1-Wire bus communication and includes a unique 64-bit serial code, allowing multiple sensors to be connected and managed in one system - ideal for multi-zone monitoring in trailers, compartments, or storage units.
The TSH202B is compatible with leading fleet management controller brands widely used in Australia, including:
Teltonika
Ruptela
Queclink
Xirgo
Backed by a 3-year warranty, the TSH202B is a cost-effective upgrade for fleets that demand performance, reliability, and confidence long after installation.

articles.title: Leadshine Stepper Motor Guide (Closed and Open-Loop)

blocks.text: A stepper motor is a type of electric motor that moves in precise steps, making it ideal for applications where accurate positioning is needed, like 3D printers, CNC machines, and robotics. Instead of rotating continuously like regular motors, it moves in small, fixed angles (steps) when electrical pulses are sent to it.

A stepper motor driver is the electronic device that controls the motor. It sends the right sequence of electrical pulses to the motor coils to make it turn the correct amount, direction, and speed. Some drivers are simple (open-loop), while others are more advanced (closed-loop), using sensors to monitor the motor's position and adjust in real time for more accurate control.

Our video for using Leadshine stepper motors and drivers walks through wiring the system, tuning driver parameters (especially for closed‑loop versus open‑loop operation), and performing a test run to verify everything is working properly.

Once the order has been processed into our accounting system, it’s time to collect the items for your order.

Our warehouse is located at Carrum Downs, where we try to keep at least 1-3 of each of our in-stock items on the shelf. Most of our customers decide to ship with Australia Post Express Post, which will travel interstate by air and aim to deliver in the next business day or so. Couriers such as TNT and Couriers Please are also available should customers need them.

Once the packages are labelled, we scan their tracking information into our system so it can be easily looked up using your order or invoice number. We also send out an email with the invoice and tracking number, so make sure you check your junk mail filters if you do not receive this email. From there, the packages are made ready to be collected by our friends at Australia Post or courier pick-up drivers. From there, the packages are out of our control, but we have done all we can to make sure that those packages are safe and secure for the journey and will arrive with you promptly.

This kind of machine cannot be purchased off the shelf and suits our business model perfectly. What’s fantastic about it as well is that, as our business grows and we start to test new products, the system can easily be updated to include new automation cycles, sensors, etc.

The Hydreon RG-11 Optical Rain Gauge is a reliable and cost-effective choice for precipitation measurements. The sensor package is about the size of a tennis ball and completely sealed from the environment. A built-in mounting arm allows for convenient mounting to weather station masts, buildings, and other infrastructure.

The Rain Gauge senses water hitting its outside surface using beams of infrared light, modeling the principle used in automotive rain-sensing windshield wiper controls. The optical gauge bounces the infrared beams within the sensor lens, and as rain drops hit the surface, the infrared light escapes through. Changes in the intensity of the infrared beams during rainfall are directly correlated with the size of the rain drop. The system automatically compensates for condensation and very small drops; it can detect rain drops less than a half millimeter in size!

Because of these features the RG-11 has been extremely popular with a wide range of customers. Last month Hydreon released two new models the RG-9 and the RG-15 and Ocean Controls have just obtained stock.
RG-9 Rain Sensor

The Hydreon RG-9 Solid State Rain Sensor is a rainfall sensing device intended to detect and communicate when a pre-selected rain intensity has been reached or exceeded. The sensitivity levels are: Rain Drops, Very Light, Medium, Heavy. The duration of the positive detection is also selectable: No Hold, Hold Time 5 Minutes, Hold Time 10 Minutes, Hold Time 15 Minutes.

The RG-9 has multiple outputs: visual output via an on-board LED, Open Collector output and RS232 serial communications that provide more detailed data, including 8 near real-time rain intensity levels and allow for reading the status and configuration of the device. Power consumption of the RG-9 is very low, and the device is well-suited to solar-power applications.
RG-15 Tipping Rain Bucket Gauge

The Hydreon RG-15 Solid State Tipping Bucket is a rainfall measuring device intended to replace conventional tipping buckets. The RG-15 is rugged, reliable, maintenance-free and features a nominal accuracy of within 10%. The RG-15 is designed to replace tipping bucket rain gauges in many applications where their maintenance requirements make them impractical.

The RG-15 uses beams of infrared light within a plastic lens about the size of a tennis ball. The round surface of the lens discourages collection of debris, and the RG-15 has no moving parts to stick, and no water-pathways to clog. The device features an open-collector output that emulates a conventional tipping bucket, as well as serial communications that provide more detailed data and allow for configuration of the device.
